Investing in Worcester County, Maryland Tax Lien Sales

Interested in a reliable investment with great returns? Consider tax lien investing in Worcester County, Maryland. With potential annual returns of 10%, it’s a smart way to diversify your portfolio. The entry costs remain relatively low compared to traditional real estate investments.

Understanding Tax Lien Certificates

The county issues tax lien certificates when property owners fail to pay their taxes. By purchasing these certificates, you pay off the delinquent taxes and, in return, earn interest until the property owner redeems the lien. If the property owner does not redeem the lien within a specified period, you may have the right to foreclose on the property and take ownership.

FAQs for Tax Liens

Q: What happens if the property owner redeems the lien? A: If the property owner redeems the lien, they must pay the outstanding taxes plus any accrued interest. As the certificate holder, you will receive your initial investment back along with the interest earned.

Q: What risks do investors face in tax lien investing?

A: The primary risk arises if the property owner does not redeem the property, making the foreclosure process costly and time-consuming. Additionally, the property could have other liens or issues.

Q: How do I register for the tax lien sale?

A: Register online through Real Auction and pay a $100 non-refundable fee.
